gaps.title: Maintenance blocking by room admins is not covered by the mockup
gaps.description: REQ-003 (room admins, the facilities team, block a room from a start to an end date and time with a reason, per DEC-004 and DEC-005) has no supporting screen, component or flow in the capture. Only the staff booking page (SCR-001) was captured; how a facilities team member creates, views, changes or removes a block, enters the reason, and sees which existing bookings will be affected is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Blocking is an approved requirement whose effect is to cancel other people's bookings and email them, so the admin-side steps and inputs must be specified, yet there is no observed design to specify from.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The facilities team's blocking workflow would be specified without customer-agreed screens or steps, and whether a block can be edited or removed after creation would be left undefined.

gaps.title: Rules for overlapping bookings and bookings that clash with a block are undefined
gaps.description: Neither the requirements nor the decisions state whether two bookings for the same room may overlap, what a staff member sees when they pick a time that is already booked, or whether a booking can be made inside an existing maintenance block. The mockup's form (SCR-002) shows no availability information and the behaviour on pressing Book was not observed.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-002] 'Can a room be booked in the past or at overlapping times; how are conflicts with existing bookings handled?'

gaps.why_it_matters: A room booking feature whose core promise is a reserved room cannot be specified without knowing whether double-booking is prevented; DEC-002 answered the duration and look-ahead limits but not clashes, and DEC-005 covers bookings that exist before a block but not attempts to book into a block afterwards.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Two staff members could hold the same room at the same time, or staff could book a room under maintenance, with no agreed rule for which booking wins.
research_questions: How do established workplace room-booking products (for example Microsoft 365 room mailboxes or Google Workspace resource calendars) handle overlapping requests for the same room by default?
What are common rules for treating back-to-back bookings (one ending exactly when the next starts) as non-overlapping?

gaps.title: Blocking cancels other people's bookings with no defined safeguard or recovery
gaps.description: DEC-005 states that existing bookings in a blocked period are cancelled and their owners emailed. It is not defined whether the facilities team member sees the affected bookings before confirming, whether a block can be undone, and whether removing or shortening a block restores any cancelled bookings. No screen for this was captured.
gaps.why_it_matters: A single admin action can cancel many staff members' bookings at once, which is a bulk, cross-user change to data those users own; DEC-003 otherwise restricts cancellation to the booking owner.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: A mistyped date range could silently cancel a large number of bookings with no way to recover them, and staff would lose rooms they relied on.
research_questions: What confirmation and undo patterns are recommended for bulk destructive actions that affect other users' records (for example GOV.UK Design System or Nielsen Norman Group guidance)?

gaps.title: Two people booking the same slot at the same moment, and repeated Book presses
gaps.description: It is not defined what happens when two staff members submit bookings for the same room and time at nearly the same moment, when a block is created while someone is mid-booking, or when Book is pressed more than once. The capture is static, so behaviour on pressing Book was not observed.
gaps.why_it_matters: Staff can book any meeting room (DEC-001), so popular rooms are likely to be contended, and a block can be created at any time by the facilities team; whatever overlap rule is agreed in GAP-002 is only meaningful if it holds under simultaneous requests.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Duplicate or overlapping bookings could be created, or a booking could be confirmed for a period that has just been blocked.
research_questions: What techniques are commonly used to guarantee that two concurrent reservation requests for the same resource and time range cannot both succeed?
How do booking systems make a create-booking request safe to retry without creating a duplicate booking?

gaps.title: Booking form validation and limit enforcement are unspecified
gaps.description: The form shows no required-field markers, and it is not defined what happens if Start is empty, in the past, or more than 30 days ahead (DEC-002), what time granularity Start accepts, where errors appear, or whether entered values are kept on error. The Duration list shows only 1, 2 and 4 hours, while REQ-001 and DEC-002 say up to 4 hours per booking; whether other durations up to 4 hours (for example 3 hours or 30 minutes) are allowed is not stated.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-002] 'Which fields are required, and what happens if Start is left empty?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The approved limits (4 hours per booking, 30 days ahead) are the only booking rules the customer has set, and the mockup does not show how a staff member is told they have broken one.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Limits could be enforced inconsistently or not at all, and the allowed durations could differ from what the customer intends.
research_questions: What does WCAG 2.2 AA (success criteria 3.3.1, 3.3.3 and 4.1.3) require for presenting form validation errors and identifying required fields?

gaps.title: Outcome states after Book and Cancel booking, and empty or loading list states, not shown
gaps.description: Only the default state of SCR-001 was captured. What staff see after a successful booking or cancellation, when booking or cancelling fails, while data is loading, and when 'My bookings' has no rows is not shown in the capture.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-002] 'What confirmation, error or failure feedback appears after pressing Book?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Booking and cancelling are the two approved staff actions, and staff need to know whether they actually hold or have released a room.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Staff may assume a booking succeeded when it failed (or the reverse), leading to missed or double-occupied meetings.
research_questions: How should success and failure status messages be announced to screen-reader users without moving focus, under WCAG 2.2 success criterion 4.1.3?

gaps.title: Cancellation confirmation, start-time cutoff in the list, and what happens to cancelled rows
gaps.description: DEC-003 settles that only the owner may cancel, at any time before the booking starts. It is not defined whether a confirmation step precedes cancellation, whether a cancellation can be undone, how the Cancel booking button behaves for a booking that has started or ended, whether past and cancelled bookings (including ones cancelled by a maintenance block) remain in 'My bookings', and whether the room is immediately bookable again.
gaps.why_it_matters: The approved cutoff (before start) must be visible and enforced in the list, and a booking cancelled by the facilities team needs to be distinguishable from one the owner cancelled.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Staff could cancel by accident with no recovery, or try to cancel bookings that are no longer cancellable, and would not see why a booking vanished after a block.

gaps.title: Content and delivery failure of the block-cancellation email
gaps.description: DEC-005 says owners of bookings cancelled by a block are emailed. What the email contains (room, time, block reason, alternatives), who sends it, whether the facilities team learns of delivery failures, and whether any other in-product notice exists are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: The email is the only agreed way a staff member learns their room was taken away; if it is not delivered they may turn up to a room under maintenance.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Staff miss cancellation notices and meetings are disrupted, with no one aware that notification failed.
research_questions: What delivery-failure signals (bounces, deferrals) do transactional email services typically expose, and how are they usually surfaced to the sending application?

gaps.title: Staff cannot see room availability or maintenance blocks before choosing a time
gaps.description: The form offers a room list (Oak, Elm) and a start time but no availability information is shown in the capture. Whether staff can see existing bookings or blocked periods for a room before submitting is not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-002] 'Is room availability shown anywhere, and does the room list depend on the user?'

gaps.why_it_matters: DEC-001 answered that staff may book any room, but finding a free slot depends on knowing what is taken or under maintenance; without that, staff learn about clashes only after pressing Book.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Booking becomes trial and error, and staff cannot plan around maintenance blocks.

gaps.title: Sign-in requirement and bookings of staff who leave or lose access
gaps.description: DEC-001 limits booking to employees with a company account, implying sign-in, but what a signed-out user or a visitor sees is not defined, nor what happens to future bookings (and their rooms) when an employee's account is disabled, or when a session expires mid-booking.

evidence_refs.locator: SCR-004 field 'Booker (owner of My bookings)' basis inferred

gaps.why_it_matters: Only the owner may cancel (DEC-003), so a departed employee's future bookings could hold rooms that nobody is permitted to release.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Rooms stay reserved for people who no longer work there, and access rules for non-staff are left to implementation.

gaps.title: Accessibility of the booking form and per-row Cancel booking actions
gaps.description: The Start field is a native date-time input and each row in 'My bookings' has a button labelled only 'Cancel booking'. Keyboard use, accessible names that identify which booking a Cancel button acts on when several rows exist, and how outcomes are announced are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: All employees may book (DEC-001), so the tool must be usable by staff relying on keyboards and screen readers; identical button labels in a list make it unclear which booking would be cancelled.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Some staff may be unable to book, or may cancel the wrong booking.
research_questions: What do WCAG 2.2 success criteria 2.4.6 and 2.5.3 require for repeated action buttons in a table, such as one 'Cancel booking' per row?
How accessible are native datetime-local inputs across current major browsers and screen readers?

gaps.title: Time zone and time granularity for Start and blocks
gaps.description: The Start input and block start and end times (DEC-005) do not state which time zone they are in, how times are shown to staff and in the cancellation email, or what minute steps are allowed.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-002] 'Is the Start time in a specific timezone, and are there time-step or granularity rules?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Overlap with other bookings and with blocks, the 30-day window and the before-start cancellation cutoff all depend on comparing times consistently, including across daylight-saving changes.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Bookings and blocks may be compared or displayed an hour out around clock changes, producing false clashes or missed ones.
research_questions: What is the recommended practice for storing and comparing room-booking times so that bookings around daylight-saving transitions are handled correctly?

gaps.title: Traceability of blocks and cancellations
gaps.description: Whether the system must record who created a block, who cancelled a booking (owner or block), when, and with what reason is not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Blocks cancel other people's bookings, so staff complaints about lost rooms can only be answered if the cause and actor are recorded.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Disputes about why a booking disappeared cannot be resolved.

gaps.title: Editing bookings, managing the room list, and retention of past bookings
gaps.description: Whether a booking can be edited rather than cancelled and rebooked, who maintains the list of rooms (Oak, Elm), and how long past or cancelled bookings are kept are not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-002] 'Can a booking be edited after creation?'
ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-003] 'What does the table show when there are no bookings, and are past bookings listed?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The facilities team already administers rooms for maintenance (DEC-004), so whether they also manage the room list affects their permissions; booking records include who booked, which is personal data subject to retention.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Room changes and booking history handling are left to implementation choices.

assumptions.text: The captured page (SCR-001) is the staff-facing booking view only; the absence of an admin blocking screen means it was not captured, not that it does not exist.
assumptions.why: Only one page was captured and REQ-003 is approved.
assumptions.impact: GAP-001 is framed as uncovered by the mockup rather than as a product limitation.
assumptions.to_confirm: Whether a design for the facilities team's blocking workflow exists.

assumptions.text: The Duration options shown (1, 2 and 4 hours) are treated as possibly incomplete rather than as a contradiction of REQ-001's 'up to 4 hours'.
assumptions.why: Neither REQ-001 nor DEC-002 lists the allowed durations.
assumptions.impact: Recorded under GAP-005 as unclear rather than as a conflict.

assumptions.text: Bookings cancelled by a maintenance block (DEC-005) are a separate path from owner cancellation and do not breach DEC-003's owner-only rule.
assumptions.why: DEC-003 says only the owner can cancel, while DEC-005 has blocks cancel bookings.
assumptions.impact: Not raised as a conflict; addressed in GAP-003 and GAP-007.
assumptions.to_confirm: That block-driven cancellation is an intended exception to owner-only cancellation.

proposed_status_changes.reason: Whether overlapping bookings for the same room, or bookings inside a maintenance block, are allowed is not stated (GAP-002).
No mockup coverage for the blocking workflow, and whether a block can be edited, removed or undone is not stated (GAP-001, GAP-003).
